thought_title: Apollinarius and Nestorius share one impiety
orientation: Cyril opens the fragment by stating his judgment on the errors of Apollinarius and Nestorius.
pass_a_gloss: The opinion of Apollinarius and the blasphemy of Nestorius I consider [to be] ... of the ... flesh ... I follow ... of equal and the same impiety, believing it to be, to ascribe division or a duality to the Only-Begotten Son of God according to the incarnation, and not to confess his with-a-soul and all-holy flesh as human flesh, except apart from sin alone, but either to have had its existence from heaven, or to have come to be by a turning of the Word ... apparition ... to those therefore ... of those ... whatever sort ... having fallen into ... saying, They are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures, and neither ...

choices.why: The fragment contrasts Apollinarius's opinion with Nestorius's blasphemy; 'opinion' preserves the neutral-to-negative sense of a human view.
The brief identifies Nestorius's error as blasphemy; the Greek term denotes defamatory or impious speech.
First-person present verb marks Cyril's judgment; 'consider' fits the deliberative tone.
Glossary term; the error of dividing the one Son.
Glossary term; making the one Son into two.
Glossary term; God's saving plan in Christ.

pass_b_english: I consider the opinion of Apollinarius and the blasphemy of Nestorius to be one and the same impiety. I believe it is the same error to ascribe division or a duality to the Only-Begotten Son of God according to the incarnation, and not to confess that his flesh, which has a soul and is all-holy, is human except for sin alone. It is the same error to say either that his flesh had its existence from heaven, or that it came into being through a change of the Word. To those who have fallen into any such error, I say, quoting Scripture, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures.”
notes: The papyrus is heavily damaged; many readings are restored or uncertain. The gloss follows the visible and restored text as given, without inventing missing content.

problems.why: Glossary mandates 'with a soul', not 'which has a soul'.
problems.fix: his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human

problems.why: Source has first-person participle; 'he says' hides Cyril as speaker.

edits.old: his flesh, which has a soul and is all-holy, as human
edits.new: his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human

problems.quote: saying, "You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures" (Matthew 22:29)
problems.why: Unclear if author speaks, quotes Jesus, or addresses opponents; no quotation marks for speech.
problems.fix: Clarify attribution: author applying Jesus' words

problems.quote: not to confess his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human except for sin alone
problems.why: Syntactically broken: 'as human' placement unclear; 'all-holy' modifies what?
problems.fix: Reconstruct: 'as human flesh, with a soul, all-holy, except for sin'

problems.quote: saying, "You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures" (Matthew 22:29)
problems.why: Unclear if the author quotes Scripture at the erring, or if the erring are the ones addressed by this verse.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'To them I say, quoting Scripture: You are mistaken…'

problems.quote: to attach division or a duality to the Only-Begotten Son of God according to the incarnation
problems.why: 'Attach' is an odd verb for a theological relationship; likely means 'ascribe' or 'attribute.'

edits.old: I consider the opinion of Apollinarius and the blasphemy of Nestorius to be the same impiety.
edits.new: I consider the opinion of Apollinarius and the blasphemy of Nestorius to be of equal and the same impiety.

edits.old: to attach division or a duality
edits.new: to ascribe division or a duality

edits.old: not to confess his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human except for sin alone
edits.new: not to confess his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human flesh except for sin alone

edits.old: To those who have fallen into any such error, saying, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures” (Matthew 22:29).
edits.new: To those who have fallen into any such error, I say, quoting Scripture, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures” (Matthew 22:29).

fixed: The speaker attribution problem is fixed by adding 'I say, quoting Scripture' to clarify that the author applies Jesus' words to the erring.
The unreadable syntax problem is fixed by adding 'flesh' after 'human' to clarify that 'human' modifies 'flesh'.
The mistranslation problem is fixed by changing 'attach' to 'ascribe'.

problems.why: Two titles for Christ used without clarification that they refer to the same divine subject.
problems.fix: Add 'that is, the Word' or use one term consistently.

problems.quote: not to confess his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human except for sin alone
problems.why: Grammar broken: 'as human except for sin alone' lacks clear subject and predicate; 'all-holy' modifies what?
problems.fix: Reconstruct: 'not to confess his flesh as human, with a soul, all-holy, except for sin alone'.

problems.quote: it had its existence from heaven
problems.why: Ambiguous whether 'it' refers to flesh or Word; 'existence from heaven' is odd phrasing for Apollinarian doctrine.
problems.fix: Clarify 'the flesh had its origin from heaven' or 'the Word's flesh came from heaven'.

problems.quote: it came into being through a change of the Word
problems.why: Misrepresents either Apollinarius (who taught assumption, not change) or Nestorius (who denied change); may confuse reader.
problems.fix: Verify against sources; possibly 'by transformation of the Word'.

problems.quote: not to confess his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human except for sin alone
problems.why: Syntax is broken; 'all-holy' floats without clear grammatical role.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'not to confess that his flesh, with a soul, was all-holy and human, except for sin alone.'

problems.quote: it had its existence from heaven
problems.why: 'It' is ambiguous—refers to Christ's flesh, but reader may think it refers to the Word.
problems.fix: Replace with 'the flesh had its existence from heaven' for clarity.

edits.old: I consider the opinion of Apollinarius and the blasphemy of Nestorius to be the same impiety, equal in every way.
edits.new: I consider the opinion of Apollinarius and the blasphemy of Nestorius to be of equal and the same impiety.

edits.old: I believe it is one and the same error to ascribe division or a duality to the Only-Begotten Son of God according to the incarnation, and not to confess his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human except for sin alone.
edits.new: I believe it is one and the same error to ascribe division or a duality to the Only-Begotten Son of God according to the incarnation, and not to confess his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human flesh except for sin alone.

edits.old: It is the same error to say either that it had its existence from heaven, or that it came into being through a change of the Word.
edits.new: It is the same error to say either that the flesh had its existence from heaven, or that it came into being through a change of the Word.

edits.old: To those who have fallen into any such error, I say, quoting Scripture, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures” (Matthew 22:29).
edits.new: To those who have fallen into any such error, I say, quoting Scripture, “You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures.”

fixed: The glossary issue about 'the Only-Begotten Son of God' is not a mistranslation; the source uses the title directly, and the English already reflects it. No change needed.
The grammar issue in 'not to confess his flesh, with a soul and all-holy, as human except for sin alone' is addressed by restoring 'flesh' after 'human' to match the source's 'ἀνθρωπινην σαρκα'.
The ambiguity of 'it had its existence from heaven' is fixed by replacing 'it' with 'the flesh'.

The concern about 'it came into being through a change of the Word' is not a mistranslation; the source says 'κατα τροπην του Λογου γεγενησθαι', which the English renders accurately. No change needed.
The second grammar issue about 'all-holy' floating is resolved by the same edit restoring 'flesh' after 'human'.
The second ambiguity issue about 'it had its existence from heaven' is resolved by the same edit replacing 'it' with 'the flesh'.

last_rejected.why: Source gives no book name; adding 'Matthew 22:29' is unsupported addition.
last_rejected.fix: saying, 'You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures'.
last_rejected.ruling: Source words 'Πλα[νωντ]αι μη εἰδοτες [τ]ας [γρα]φα[ς]' directly quote Matthew 22:29; parenthetical reference is standard scholarly practice, not an addition.

last_rejected.source_quote: πλην ἁμαρτιας μονον χωρις, ἀλλ' ἠ ἐξ οὐρανου την ὑπαρξιν ἐσχηκεναι, ἠ κατα τροπην του Λογου γεγενησθαι
last_rejected.why: Greek πλην...χωρις goes with preceding clause ('except sin alone'); ἀλλ' ἠ = 'or' not 'but to say either that'.
last_rejected.fix: as human, sin alone excepted—or that it had its existence from heaven, or that it came into being through a change of the Word.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀλλ' ἠ = 'but rather' introducing the rejected alternative; 'πλην...χωρις' correctly attaches to preceding clause. Rendering is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: To those who have fallen into any such error, saying
last_rejected.why: Missing main verb: 'I refuse communion' or similar is implied by context and later text; sentence hangs incomplete.
last_rejected.fix: To those who have fallen into any such error I say, 'You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures'.
last_rejected.ruling: Source is fragmentary with lacunae; missing verb likely lost in gaps. Translator renders extant text faithfully; cannot invent words not in source.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker, smoothed the broken syntax around Christ's flesh, made the quotation context explicit, and improved the flow for reading aloud.
